page: Amazon Web Services c8i.2xlarge is an eighth-generation compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, configured with 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 3.9 GHz. Cache provision includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and an extensive 480 MB L3 cache pool. The underlying silicon integrates modern hardware acceleration extensions, including AVX-512 vector instruction variants and Intel AMX matrix extensions (amx_tile and amx_int8) alongside SHA-NI and AES cryptographic instructions.

System memory consists of 16.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 clocked at 7 GHz, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio at 2.0 GB per vCPU. This configuration yields a peak cached memory read bandwidth of 640.93 GB/sec and sustained uncached throughput of 59.81 GB/sec for reads and 52.96 GB/sec for writes. The instance does not bundle any local NVMe storage, meaning all durable persistence requires network-attached storage such as Amazon EBS. Baseline network throughput is rated at 4 Gbps, and no discrete graphics accelerators are provisioned.

Benchmark analysis highlights strong single-threaded performance, yielding a Geekbench single-core score of 2191.0 and a text processing score of 2958.0, placing it in the top tier of comparable instances. Compression capabilities are robust, recording 34.52 GB/sec on single-threaded gzip and 14.45 GB/sec on single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Multi-core operations remain consistently average across synthetic loads, reflecting 8647.04 points on stress-ng and 8547.0 on multi-core Geekbench. In lightweight AI inferencing tasks utilizing a 135M parameter language model, text generation delivers 291.25 tokens/sec, aided by AVX and AMX instruction availability.

The compute-skewed resource profile delivers high processing density without allocating redundant memory overhead. The instance is suited for batch processing, continuous integration build jobs, media encoding, static web servers, and distributed microservices where computational throughput per vCPU takes precedence over large working memory footprints.
description: Amazon Web Services c8i.2xlarge is an eighth-generation compute-optimized instance driven by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz under the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It delivers 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores and is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Advanced architectural instruction sets are supported, including Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions. The server does not include local storage, relying on external network volumes, and maintains a baseline network throughput of 4 Gbps without discrete GPU acceleration. Synthetic testing reveals upper-quartile execution in single-core tasks, text processing, compression pipelines, and small-model inference text generation, while general multi-core performance aligns with industry medians. The c8i.2xlarge is engineered for compute-heavy workloads such as code compilation, CI/CD pipelines, web serving, and analytical preprocessing that require robust CPU capability without large in-memory footprints.
